carried_from: data/y-genesis-navigation-v1.js · color_contract · generated 2026-07-18, a presentation fixture whose roles v1 carried forward; v1's three roles are carried forward again here and two are added

who_decided_what.the_ledger: Exodus names the materials — tekhelet, argaman, tola'at shani, shesh — and gold beside them, over and over, and never once says what any of them looked like.
who_decided_what.the_owner: Which material carries which channel, ruled on 2026-09-10. Gold is not a final color: it is an in-process color — huds, boxes, the frame — the way the gold in the tabernacle was worked into the blue that is actually shown. That leaves purple for this project's own voice.
who_decided_what.this_page: Every hex value below, and every one before it. A role is recorded; a hex is a tradition, and the traditions disagree. No reader should come away thinking a hex code is attested — only that a channel was assigned, by a person, on a date.

channels.rule: A channel is not a decoration. It says who is speaking. The corpus speaks in tola'at shani, its reading speaks in tekhelet, this project speaks in argaman, and gold is only ever the frame around one of them.

text_as_written.carries: The Hebrew of the corpus, the letters as the source has them. Carried as a wash behind the letters and not in them: since 2026-09-10 every glyph on this page is argaman, and the ink says nothing about whose words these are.
text_as_written.how_it_is_carried: A wash the width of the word, under the glyph. It lifts while the reader is holding the word and comes back when they let go.
text_as_written.reads_as: the ink the Hebrew is written in, a quiet rose-red, with nothing behind the letters
text_as_written.held_as: muted: the material at a lower saturation than a glyph in it would be painted at, so a page of it is a page of words and not of color
text_as_written.dim_as: The dim red (--shani-dim) is never a word: it is the rail along a commentary, the edge of a source's tag, and the maqaf between a compound's pieces on a card's head in a work whose Masoretic marks are not drawn in gold (where they are, the maqaf is a mark and gold, on the line and on the card alike).

reading_as_shown.carries: The reading offered for a word: the English that comes from a dictionary this project holds a license to. Someone else's words about the corpus. Carried as a wash, the same as the corpus's own channel, because both are provenance and neither is ink.
reading_as_shown.note: Named and deliberately unused until today. v1 recorded that keeping it unused meant the day it appeared would be a decision somebody made rather than a color that crept in. This is that day, and the decision is recorded above.
reading_as_shown.how_it_is_carried: A wash behind the reading in a book. On the door, where a whole card IS one book's reading, the card carries it and the reading inside is not washed twice.
reading_as_shown.reads_as: the ink the reading is written in, a quiet blue, inside a gold hairline so it stays a label
reading_as_shown.held_as: muted: the material at a lower saturation than a glyph in it would be painted at, so a page of it is a page of words and not of color
reading_as_shown.pressed_as: One blue at two shades, a regular and a dim, and no bold (the owner, 2026-10-10: "id probably go regular and dim. i dont like our bold that much"; this supersedes 2026-10-03, "similar to our logo id have 2 blues: a bold and a regular", whose "maybe the letters bold too" stands as the weight). A reading at rest and a reading pressed are the same regular blue (--tekhelet). Pressed, it is worn bold inside the pressed cell (channels.reader_selection.pressed_cell), 3.83:1 on the pressed linen, the same as the open word's reading on the line. Never a blue fill.
reading_as_shown.dim_as: The dim blue (--tekhelet-dim) is never a reading: it is only the + between a reading's parts, which it tells apart from a + inside a reading's own words.

our_own_voice.carries: Sentences this project wrote: rule statements, counting notes, captions, obligation lines, what a demonstration says about itself, and every line saying a record holds nothing here. This is the page's INK — all of it — so our voice is the unmarked case and everything a reader sees marked is a departure from us into someone else's words.
our_own_voice.why: The owner's ruling. Once red is the text and blue is the reading, the project's own prose is the one voice left without a material, and it is the voice a reader most needs to be able to tell apart from the other two.
our_own_voice.how_it_is_carried: The ink, everywhere, in two purples and no more (the owner, 2026-10-10: "personally i dont see a gain from more than 2/2/2/2 and 3 linen"; "titles get regular and text gets dim ... id probably go regular and dim"): the regular (--argaman) for titles, values and what is under the reader's hand; the dim (--argaman-dim) for running text, notes, labels, and links and controls at rest, held at body-text contrast. A line saying something is absent, withheld, refused or does not reconcile is the dim, in italic where it stands in for a name or a value; the saturated argaman it had of its own from 2026-09-10 is folded in.
our_own_voice.reads_as: the ink itself — every glyph on the page is this

structure.carries: The spine: titles, coordinates, the names of parts and chapters. The frame a reading sits in.
structure.in_process: Gold never terminates. It is the box, never the thing in the box, and a word is never left gold — it resolves into a text color or a reading color.
structure.reads_as: line work only: rules, borders, boxes, never ink at rest

reader_selection.carries: What this reader has opened, chosen, pressed or armed among the page's own controls: the verse number the address names, the mode pressed, the chapter opened. Nothing wears it at rest, and no word wears it at all.
reader_selection.in_process: A selection is the most in-process thing on the page, so the page's own controls take the regular gold at their edge while the reader's hand is on them, drawn twice as heavy when pressed; at rest every edge is the dim gold (the owner, 2026-10-10: "id probably go regular and dim"). Words are not controls: what a reader sees under a held word is the word's own channel, weighted, never gold.
reader_selection.held_apart_from_structure_by: Hue and weight. Structure is gold and does not move; a selection is purple, bold, and the only thing on the page that appears and disappears under the reader's hand.
reader_selection.moved_from: v1 valued this electric_blue, and from 2026-09-09 it was gold at its amber value. Blue became the reading, so a blue selection said "selected" and "English" in one color; then the owner, 2026-10-03, on amber pills: "idk if turning purple to gold is a clear way to highlight toggle pills et al, maybe bold purple would be better?" A pressed control is now this project's own purple, worn bold. From 2026-10-10 it is the regular purple itself, worn bold; the press is carried by the weight and the pressed cell, not by a purple deeper than the ink.
reader_selection.reads_as: ink on the page's own controls under the reader's hand, worn bold, and gone when they let go; a held word keeps its own ink inside a gold box
reader_selection.held_word: A word the reader is holding is boxed in gold — the whole block, Hebrew and reading together, an outline three pixels out — and the card is that box projected forward: two gold lines from the box's far corners to the card's near corners. Nothing is filled and no ink changes (owner, 2026-09-11, drawn on a screenshot). The box and its lines are the regular gold, the gold of the hand; a held word never takes the purple of a pressed control.
reader_selection.held_apart_from_our_voice_by: Weight and behavior: our voice at rest is the regular weight of the page's ink; a selection is the same purple pressed bold, and only while it is pressed.
reader_selection.pressed_cell: One rule for every pressed or highlighted cell, pill or control (the owner, 2026-10-03: "i wouldnt retrace pills from gold to blue. you keep jumping rules. id: 1. darken the linen backdrop on a highlighted cell, 2. bolden the gold, 3. bolden the blue text"): its border stays gold, drawn twice as heavy; its linen darkens one step (--press-wash); its letters are bold in their own ink at its regular shade: the regular blue for a reading, the purple for a control (the owner, 2026-10-10: "i dont like our bold that much"; the bold is the weight, not a deeper color). No cell is ever filled with a color.

faces.rule: One face. The courtyard: linen hangings in daylight. There is nothing here for a reader to choose and nothing kept on the device.

day.commentary_set_apart_by: Its red rail and its frame, not a ground of its own. The commentary's parchment, decided 2026-09-10 and carried from the v1 fixture, was folded into the ground on 2026-10-10 under the owner's three linens ("personally i dont see a gain from more than 2/2/2/2 and 3 linen").
day.linens: Three, and no more (the owner, 2026-10-09: "maybe linen should have 3 shades?"; 2026-10-10: "personally i dont see a gain from more than 2/2/2/2 and 3 linen"): the ground (--bg), on which the page, a card, a pill, a panel and a commentary at rest stand; the cell (--cell-wash), a glaze laid on the ground behind a word and its reading, which a hover and a chip also wear; and the pressed linen (--press-wash), which every pressed cell wears and the blob between a word and its English shares. A glaze is never laid on another glaze, and a veil of the ground is the ground.

faces.what_was_dropped: The tent's dark face, a purple ground under its coverings, which v1 and v2 both carried and this edition served until today. The owner dropped it. It is not deprecated or left behind a flag: the palette, the toggle, the stored preference and every rule written for it are gone, because a half-removed face paints some elements from a palette nothing else uses, and that is worse than either state.
faces.what_this_costs: A reader whose device is set to dark now gets linen. color-scheme is declared light so the browser does not hand its own dark chrome to a light page. Nothing about the channels moved: they were tuned on this face, and this is the face that was called right.
faces.note: The two-faced rule read: 'the courtyard hangings are linen in daylight, and the tent is dark under its coverings.' Half of that sentence described something this edition no longer does, so the sentence went rather than being left standing over an absence.

note: Linen is not glare: the day ground sits below paper white and its ink is warm, not black. Shesh is the cloth the whole page is written in, which is why it is the neutral and not a channel.
what_changed_after_v2_was_written: On 2026-09-11 the held word stopped taking amber: it deepens its own wash instead (channels.reader_selection.held_word), and amber stays with the page's own controls. On 2026-09-11, off six mockups rendered on the real page, the owner chose the fourth: the ink carries the channel again, held muted — Hebrew in a quiet rose-red, its reading in a quiet blue with a gold hairline, no wash behind either — and the page's one ink, argaman, stays on everything that is ours. The held word lifts (a touch larger, a soft shadow) and the card pops out from under it; nothing held is filled. The washes of 2026-09-10 are retired; the one place a channel is filled is the pressed pill on the card, which is the reading's own ink with the linen for letters. Later on 2026-09-11 the held word stopped lifting and took the gold box instead, with the two projection lines to the card; the readings lost their boxes; the Hebrew at the head of the card is the same rose as on the line. On 2026-10-10 the palette was folded to two of each color and three linens (the owner: "personally i dont see a gain from more than 2/2/2/2 and 3 linen"; "id probably go regular and dim. i dont like our bold that much"; "my main point is uniform coloring between logo and site"). Gold is two: the dim at rest on every frame, chip and line, on the Masoretic marks and on the and of the name; the regular under the reader's hand. The amber, the name's own brighter gold and the hover's brown are gone. The purple is two: the regular for titles, values and what is pressed, the dim for running text, notes, labels and links. The red and the blue are two each, and a pressed reading is the regular blue worn bold. The woven name is dyed in the same pairs.
